title: Ledger Coding Reference — Corrections and Hardship Adjustments on a Charge Whose Payment Was Returned, Patient Financial Account
content:
**Entry.** On the Patient Financial Account, the covered returned amount of a returned-payment replacement is reduced by what has since been taken off the charge the most recently returned check or ACH payment had paid:

1. by the adjustments coded as a billing error correction posted to that charge, when there are any;
2. otherwise, by the adjustments coded as a hardship adjustment posted to it, when there are any;
3. by nothing otherwise.

**Identifying the charge.** The most recently returned check or ACH payment is the payment reversal of a check or ACH payment with the latest date on the ledger. The payment it reversed was applied to one charge; that charge is the one whose adjustments are read.

**Only one kind is taken.** The two kinds are not added together: when billing error corrections exist on the charge, their total is the reduction and hardship adjustments on the same charge are not counted.

| Billing error corrections on the charge | Hardship adjustments on the charge | Reduction |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes or no | total of the billing error corrections |
| no | yes | total of the hardship adjustments |
| no | no | nothing |

**Hypothetical examples.**

- The returned check had paid a charge that later received a billing error correction of 35.00 and a hardship adjustment of 50.00: the reduction is 35.00.
- The same charge with only the hardship adjustment of 50.00: the reduction is 50.00.
- A charge with neither: no reduction.
